plan: Queue offlane as primary. It is Mr_Meat31's best role at 54.5% over 141 games (overall is 51.6%). Set support as secondary, not the other way around.
Comfort-hero rule for the climb: Murdock. Compared with the average player on the same hero, Mr_Meat31 wins about 5.1 more games per 100 on it.
Mr_Meat31's champion pool is 12+ heroes wide and the top three are only 40% of the games. Gold-to-Platinum climbs are almost always pool-narrowing stories: aim for 70%+ of games on the top three.
The math: Mr_Meat31 is at 724 VP; Platinum III starts at 900. The all-time peak is 867.
honesty: personal winrates are shrunk toward the player's own average (small heater samples do not count as mains)
field baselines are all-ranks aggregates from our current-patch match sample, not Gold-bracket-specific yet
winrate edges are observational; they say where the player wins, not why

insights.title: The tilt tax is real for Mr_Meat31
insights.finding: Right after a loss Mr_Meat31 wins 22%; right after a win, 70%. One cooldown break after losses is free VP.
insights.receipt: 2/9 after losses vs 7/10 after wins, last 20 games

insights.title: Murdock is the long-term relationship
insights.finding: 150 games and Mr_Meat31 genuinely out-pilots the field on Murdock — about 5.1 more wins per 100 games than the average Murdock player. The hours show.

insights.title: Xeebs brings out Mr_Meat31's best
insights.finding: Mr_Meat31's record alongside Xeebs is 55% over 257 ranked games — the strongest pairing in the stack. When only two of the squad queue, make it this pair.

insights.title: For the group chat
insights.finding: 1 pentakill in real 5v5s and a longest spree of 19 (plus 13 more in ARAM and brawls — the group chat can rule on whether those count). Mr_Meat31 has receipts.

coachReasoning.assessment: Mr_Meat31 has been winning fights and paying too much for them — the Murdock game that finished 10/6/4 doubled the 3-death norm and still lost, while the only win in the set (Phase 0/0/6) was the game with zero deaths against a 2 norm. The lever is banking the lead once Murdock has it instead of buying the next kill.
plan: On Murdock, place Static Trap on the retreat path before the fight starts rather than into the middle of it. The traps root whoever chases, and that is the difference between the 10 kills in the 10/6/4 game turning into a win and turning into 6 deaths.
On Murdock, take the finishing shot from distance: Long Arm of the Law travels through everything with no range limit and ignores physical armor, so there is no reason to walk forward to land it.
On Murdock, treat Hot Pursuit as the exit. Its cooldown resets on a takedown, so the speed that arrives after a kill is there to leave with — both Murdock games ran over the 3-death norm, at 6 and 4.

On Dekker, use Containment Fence as a wall between the diving enemy and the team's carry, not as a cage around one target. Lead with Photon Disruptor's slow and then land Stasis Bomb from range, since its stun grows the further the bomb travels. The 2/1/12 game already had 25 wards against a 10 norm — the fights are the part still missing.

On Grux, low health is not the signal to back out: Double Pain restores health for every enemy hero it hits and gives back more the lower Grux is, so swing it through the group first and disengage second.

insights.title: Kills were never the problem
insights.finding: The 10/6/4 Murdock game was a loss and the 0/0/6 Phase game was the win. The two Murdock losses ran 6 and 4 deaths against a 3 norm; the win came with none against a 2 norm.

insights.title: Stop the night after two losses
insights.finding: Right after a loss Mr_Meat31 wins 22%; right after a win, 70%. The reviewed set is four losses in a row, so stopping after the second loss of a night protects more VP than playing through it.

insights.title: Murdock is the real weapon
insights.finding: 150 games at 59.3%, and marginal games on Murdock are priced at +1.8 wins per 100. Those two recent Murdock losses were death-count games rather than damage games — 6 and 4 against a 3 norm.

insights.title: Offlane is the priced move
insights.finding: Offlane is worth +2.9 wins per 100 over the usual mix with 141 games of evidence, and Grux — an offlane and jungle fighter — sits at 55.4% over 56 games. When the fill lands there, that pick already works.
